root_cause: The independent timed exact-phone review (round 18, A, film eefad941) rejected the measured cut for two mandatory modern observations. In s3 (12.4 to 17.2 s) the creek water is a flat calm sheet and the car sits level with only a slow drift, so 'swept into Salado Creek' is not performed. In s8 (40.0 to 47.6 s) one wide parking-lot composition holds for 7.6 s, the declared close limits-tag shot is a relabel of the same view, and the cars sit in a thin strip with about 45 percent empty asphalt.
repair: s3: lock the camera on fixed bank landmarks (a limestone ledge and a live oak on the bank) and start the car at the low crossing or shallow bank edge, so the current visibly pushes it off that edge and carries it across a large share of the frame past those fixed landmarks within the n3 clause, with a bow wave on its upstream side and the waterline climbing the doors. s8: replace the relabelled wide-lot close with a newly staged low close composition with new content, the weather limits tag clipping onto the cord in the foreground and the nearest roof pod with its check filling a large share of the frame, cut inside 4 seconds, and refill the wide lot so the cars fill the frame. Words, claims, narration, voice take, measured captions and scene starts unchanged.
mechanism_change: The creek changes from a following camera on a car in a brown sheet to a locked camera with fixed landmarks past which the car is displaced by the current, and the s8 close changes from a rescaled view of the same lot drawing to a separately staged foreground composition.
expected_visible_result: At phone size the creek car visibly travels across the frame past fixed bank landmarks within n3, and s8 cuts from the wide lot to a distinct foreground close of the tag on its cord and a checked roof pod within four seconds.
